tiers.title: Petty Warrant
tiers.text: A name shouted at a muster roll. Bring them in and the clerk will not ask twice.

tiers.title: Standing Warrant
tiers.text: Trained, blooded and worth the rope. Their company will want them back.

tiers.title: Sealed Warrant
tiers.text: A specialist. Take the escort apart first; they will not surrender while it stands.

tiers.title: Crown Warrant
tiers.text: A second-in-command with a price on the head and a guard around it.

tiers.title: Blood Warrant
tiers.text: A field commander. Expect a full platoon between you and the writ.

tiers.title: Iron Warrant
tiers.text: A champion. The last warrant the board will ever issue, and the only one that pays like this.

notes.capture: A warrant pays for a living prisoner. Break the target to a quarter of its health or rout it, then subdue it hand to hand with an adjacent unit. Kill it and the warrant closes unpaid.
notes.ceiling: The board never names a target above seven stars. Eight-star greater elites, nine-star lords and ten-star deities are not taken with a writ; they arrive by ritual, fusion or the recruitment hall.
notes.duplicates: The copies a warrant pays are physical cards. A deck may only run as many copies of a card as the holding actually owns, so warrants are how a player deepens a line rather than merely unlocking it.
notes.bias: The board favours targets the player is already short of for the deck they field, so the warrants read as useful rather than random.
